title: Smoothness is etale local on the source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\{h_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ a jointly surjective family (every point of $X$ is the image of a point of some $U_i$) of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if each composite $f\circ h_i$ is smooth. No separatedness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. In particular, if $h:U\to X$ is etale, then $f$ is smooth at $h(u)$ if and only if $f\circ h$ is smooth at $u$: smooth at a point means smooth on an open neighbourhood of that point.

source.place: Tag 036U, lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source; etale covers are smooth covers. The pointwise assertion follows by restricting to open smooth loci and using openness of etale maps (Tag 01UA).

proof.text: For the forward implication, each etale morphism h_i is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Since f is smooth, the composite f∘h_i is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition].

source.place: Tag 02GK (morphisms-lemma-etale-smooth-unramified: an etale morphism is smooth) and Tag 01VA (morphisms-lemma-composition-smooth: composition of smooth morphisms is smooth).

proof.text: For the reverse implication, each h_i is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Hence its image W_i=h_i(U_i) is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and the W_i cover X by joint surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], h_i factors uniquely through a map q_i:U_i→W_i; this factor is surjective because W_i is the image. Restricting a flat, locally finitely presented morphism to an open source and open target preserves those properties by the local definitions. The open restriction f|_{W_i} is the $f_{U,V}$ construction of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] with target open $V=S$. The composite of q_i with f|_{W_i} is f∘h_i, so the hypothesis makes it smooth. Applying [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to q_i shows that f|_{W_i} is smooth.

source.place: Tag 036U, with Tags 01UA and 05B5: open images of etale maps and descent of smoothness along flat surjective locally finitely presented covers.

proof.text: The W_i form an open cover of X, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] says that smoothness is local on such a source cover. Since every restriction f|_{W_i} is smooth, f is smooth. This proves the global equivalence without separatedness, quasi-compactness, or Noetherian assumptions.

source.place: Tag 01V6, smoothness local on an open cover of the source.

proof.text: For the pointwise clause, suppose first that f is smooth on an open neighbourhood of h(u). The open restriction of f to that neighbourhood is the restriction described in [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Restricting h to the inverse image of that neighbourhood gives an etale map, hence a smooth map by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], and [lem-trf-smooth-composition] gives smoothness of f∘h near u. Conversely, if f∘h is smooth on an open neighbourhood V of u, then h(V) is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and contains h(u). The restriction h|_V factors through h(V) by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; it is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation. Its composite with f|_{h(V)} is smooth, so [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] gives smoothness of f|_{h(V)}. Thus f is smooth at h(u).

source.place: Tag 036U with Tag 01UA: restriction to smooth loci and openness of etale maps give the pointwise formulation.
